note: RM-005 C1 pixel oracle: the two Skybox textures rendered through the same
geometry, camera and sampler state at 1:1, once from the authored JPEG and
once from the KTX2/ETC1S transcode, and differenced in the framebuffer.
This is the only measurement in the sprint that looks at what a user sees
rather than at what the files contain.
Same shape as B4's resize-oracle.json, and not committable as a test for
the same reason: it needs BOTH versions of a file present, and the point of
the sprint is that one of them stops existing. Run once, from a temporary
suite under tests/browser/, chromium with SwiftShader, then deleted.
WHAT DECIDED THE SPRINT
Ground_4K passes and is transcoded. RMS 1.098 against the 3.0 that B4's
codecRms gate uses, a 99th percentile of 5, and its worst pixels are
0.178% speckle rather than structure. Its file falls 58 KB -> 10 KB, which
looked alarming - 0.08 bits per pixel, fifteen times lower than any other
texture in the pass - and the oracle is what turned that from a worry into
a number. The image is genuinely low-detail: B4 downscaled it from 4096 to
1024 with a Lanczos filter, and what came out is smooth enough that ETC1S
has very little to lose.
Garden refuses and stays a JPEG. A 95th percentile AT the visibility
threshold and 4.078% of channels past it is not outliers, it is banding -
in a photograph of sky, which is the content ETC1S handles worst and the
surface a first-person viewer looks at longest. Refusing costs 2.00 MB of
the 6.00 MB projected for this pair; taking it would have cost the picture.
That per-asset split is B1's rule rather than a new one: a model that could
not match the pixel tier shipped unquantised and the decision was recorded
per file. See REFUSED in tools/encode-textures.mjs, which now carries the
same numbers so a re-run cannot quietly re-encode it.
UASTC would fix the banding and is ruled out by a different budget: roughly
1.4 MB on disk against Garden's 250 KB, and public-total has 280 KB spare.
HOW TO READ THE COLUMNS
rms/p95/p99/max are absolute per-channel differences over RGB, 0-255.
pctOver8 is the share of channels differing by more than 8, which is about
where a difference stops being arithmetic and starts being visible on a
gradient. transcodedTo is three's format constant for what SwiftShader
actually transcoded to - 37492 is COMPRESSED_RGB8_ETC2.
